I need to fix three project management bugs in a TypeScript/Next.js application.

I am analyzing the codebase to fix these bugs. The first issue concerns project keys and addresses: every project in a workspace has its own key, including archived ones. When a key is already in use, it should be made unique by appending a number and trimming to four characters.

Archived project addresses remain reserved, so new projects receive different ones and archived projects can be restored under their original address. Only live projects count against the plan's project limit. Archiving frees a slot immediately, while restoring requires available capacity and is refused if the plan is full.

Restoring an archived project preserves its exact prior state and leaves archived issues archived. Only archived projects may be restored; restoring a live project is refused without notice. The workspace projects meter updates immediately after any restore, and periodic recounting stays consistent.

New issues may only be created in active projects. Paused or completed projects refuse new issues without notice, though existing issues remain editable.

A project can be marked completed only when no issues are open. Done, canceled, and archived issues do not count as open. Marking a project paused is always allowed, and reactivating it is also allowed. Marking an already completed project again does nothing.
